descriptionChirho: A general point or stretch of time, a period or moment, with no special nuance of appointment or propriety.
The proper, fitting, or appointed time for something to happen; often with pronominal suffix (in its time/season).
Temporal demonstrative use, typically with preposition כְּ, meaning 'at/about this time' or 'now'.
Occurrences or instances, 'times' in the sense of frequency or repetition rather than temporal period.
Textual variant (ketiv) read as the adverb 'now' (עַתָּה), functioning as a temporal adverb rather than the noun 'time'.
